verdict.label: BUY / SELECTIVE — Weekend Reflection: Strongest Month-End Setup of the Series, One Unsigned Binary
verdict.rationale_short: Markets are closed (Saturday). No new prints since Friday's record close. This is a reflection briefing: the week ended with SPX at a ninth-straight-weekly record (7,580.06), the 30Y below 5.0% for the first time since May 14, and oil posting its worst month since March 2020 on Iran-ceasefire optimism. The BUY framework is structurally the strongest of the series — but the single unresolved variable is binary and live this weekend: the US-Iran MoU sits on Trump's desk unsigned. Conviction holds at medium, not high, because (1) the Iran signature is a true weekend binary, (2) Day 2 of the 30Y-below-5.0% confirmation sequence cannot print until Monday, and (3) Warsh's first FOMC (June 16-17) with PCE at 3.8% remains the structural gate no rally has cleared.

bear_case: A reflection briefing on a closed Saturday is the moment to be most skeptical of a nine-week win streak. Every favorable binary is now priced — AI capex (DELL +33%), rate relief (30Y 4.97%), and an Iran deal that is still only on Trump's desk, not signed. The deal as reported is being characterized as a win for Iran: it reopens Hormuz and starts talks but locks in no constraint on Iran's enriched-uranium stockpile, which means the 60-day clock can expire with nuclear risk fully intact and oil's entire ~20% repricing reversing. Friday's 30Y sub-5.0% close was mechanically aided by month-end bond buying on the last trading day of May; the 5-day average is still above 5.0%, so the regime-clearing read rests on one assisted print. Invalidation level: if Trump publicly rejects the MoU this weekend and Brent gaps above $97 in Sunday-night futures, the BUY framework converts to Step Aside at Monday's open; a daily SPX close below 7,460 with the 30Y back above 5.10% confirms it.
